intro: Conditions without «si»: almost all of these connectors take the subjunctive.
p.siempre que.consejo: With the subjunctive it means «only if»: «siempre que me lo devuelvas». With the indicative it means «every time that».
p.con tal de que.consejo: It sets a minimum condition and asks for the subjunctive: «con tal de que llegues pronto».
p.a condición de que.consejo: It is more formal than «siempre que» and also asks for the subjunctive.
p.a no ser que.consejo: It means «except if» and asks for the subjunctive. It equals «a menos que».
p.a menos que.consejo: It means the same as «a no ser que» and asks for the subjunctive: «a menos que llueva».
p.salvo que.consejo: It also means «except if» and asks for the subjunctive: «salvo que llueva».
p.en caso de que.consejo: It anticipates a possibility and asks for the subjunctive: «en caso de que haya problemas».
p.por si.consejo: It takes the indicative: «llévate el paraguas por si llueve». It prepares for a possibility.
p.como.consejo: With the subjunctive it is a warning: «como no estudies, suspenderás». With the indicative it means «because».
p.siempre y cuando.consejo: It is a more emphatic form of «siempre que» and asks for the subjunctive.
p.de lo contrario.consejo: It means «if not». It introduces a consequence: «llega pronto; de lo contrario, no cenarás».
p.gasolina.consejo: It is feminine: «la gasolina». It is what fills the car's tank.
b1.texto:
These connectors set a condition without using **si**. Almost all take the **subjunctive**:

- **Only if**: siempre que, siempre y cuando, con tal de que, a condición de que.
- **Except if**: a no ser que, a menos que, salvo que.
- **In case**: en caso de que.
- **Warning**: como + subjunctive.

Example: Te lo presto **siempre que** me lo **devuelvas**. Iré, **a no ser que llueva**.
b2.f0.texto: Will you lend me your car on Saturday?
b2.f1.texto: Yes, as long as you give it back on Sunday.
b2.f2.texto: Of course, unless there is a lot of traffic.
b2.f3.texto: In case you have any problem, call me.
b2.f4.texto: I will take the charger in case I run out of battery.
b2.f5.texto: And if you bring it back without petrol, I will not lend it to you again.
b2.f6.texto: Don't worry, I will return it with a full tank.
b2.f7.texto: Then, unless the weather changes, we have a deal.
b4.texto:
With these connectors, the verb goes in the **present subjunctive** if the condition is open and in the **imperfect subjunctive** if it is imagined:

- Iré **a no ser que llueva**. / Iría **a no ser que lloviera**.
- **En caso de que haya** problemas, llámame.
- **Como no estudies**, suspenderás.

Two connectors take the **indicative**:

- **Por si**: llévate el paraguas **por si llueve**.
- **Salvo si** and **excepto si**, which behave like **si**.

Watch the mood:

- **Siempre que** + indicative means «every time that»: siempre que voy, llueve.
- **Como** + indicative gives a cause: como llegas tarde, me voy.
b4.e0.texto: I will lend it to you as long as you give it back.
b4.e1.texto: I will go unless it rains.
b4.e2.texto: Take the umbrella in case it rains.
b5.titulo: On the road to the coast
b5.f0.texto: The car waits by the kerb with its windows misted up.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía leaves the keys in the palm of Pablo's hand.
b5.f2.texto: The metal is cold and smells faintly of petrol.
b5.f3.texto: A thin mist covers the road and dims the colours of dawn.
b5.f4.texto: Pablo adjusts the mirror carefully and breathes deeply before starting.
b5.f5.texto: The engine starts with a soft, steady purr.
b5.f6.texto: If there is no traffic, he will reach the coast before noon.
b5.f7.texto: The fields pass on both sides like green and golden sheets.
b5.f8.texto: On the back seat, the rucksack holds a charger in case the battery fails.
b5.f9.texto: The road stretches towards the sea like a grey ribbon.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That would be «siempre que llueva»: just the opposite.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes! «A no ser que» sets an exception.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It does not give a cause: it gives an exception to what came before.
b7.frase: Te lo presto siempre que me lo ____.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: conditional «siempre que» asks for the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: With the indicative, «siempre que» means «every time that».
b7.o2.refuerzo: After these connectors the future is not used.
b7.pregunta: You set a condition. Which form is missing?
b8.frase: Llevaré el cargador por si me quedo sin batería
b8.traduccion: I will take the charger in case I run out of battery
b9.o0: Llévate el paraguas por si llueve.
b9.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Por si» goes with the indicative.
b9.o1: Llévate el paraguas por si llueva.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Por si» does not take the present subjunctive.
b9.o2: Llévate el paraguas por si lloverá.
b9.o2.refuerzo: After «si» the future is not used either.
b9.pregunta: Which sentence with «por si» is correct?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Estudias» would give a cause, not a warning.
b10.o1.refuerzo: The future does not follow conditional «como».
b10.o2.refuerzo: That's it: «como» plus subjunctive warns of what will happen.
b10.pregunta: You warn of a consequence. Which form is missing?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I will go, unless it rains.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: Well done! With the indicative it speaks of something that repeats.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Solo si» would ask for the subjunctive: «siempre que vaya».
b12.o2.refuerzo: An exception is said with «a no ser que».
b12.pregunta: «Siempre que voy, llueve». What does «siempre que» mean?
p.dejas.consejo: From «dejar». The j is silent in «dejar»; with «tú» it takes -as.
p.devuelvas.consejo: The present subjunctive of «devolver». It is used after «que».
p.tengas.consejo: The subjunctive of «tener». With «que» it means «you have».
p.problema.consejo: It is masculine even ending in -a: el problema.
p.llevaré.consejo: Future of «llevar», first person. The accent is at the end.
p.dejo.consejo: From «dejar». I let or I leave.
p.devolveré.consejo: The future of «devolver». The accent is at the end.
p.depósito.consejo: The stress falls on PO, the first vowel after the p.
p.lleno.consejo: The ll sounds like y: YE-no.
p.cambie.consejo: After «a menos que» the verb goes in the subjunctive.
p.trato.consejo: Here it means an agreement, not the «trato» of treating someone.
p.iré.consejo: The future of «ir», first person. The accent is at the end.
p.llueva.consejo: The ll sounds like y, and «ue» is one syllable.
p.llévate.consejo: The pronoun -te goes at the end of the command.
p.acera.consejo: The c before e is th in Spain; the r is a soft tap.
p.ventanillas.consejo: The v sounds like b, and ll sounds like y.
p.empañadas.consejo: The ñ sounds like ny: em-pa-NYA-das.
p.palma.consejo: It is also a palm tree; here it means the inside of the hand.
p.apaga.consejo: From «apagar». The g before a is a hard g.
p.ajusta.consejo: The j sounds like h: a-HUS-ta.
p.motor.consejo: The stress is on the last syllable, so it has no accent.
p.ronroneo.consejo: A soft, steady sound, like a cat. The rr is strong.
p.lados.consejo: Plural of «lado»; the d between vowels is soft.
p.láminas.consejo: The accent is on the first syllable.
p.doradas.consejo: The d between vowels is soft.
p.falla.consejo: The ll sounds like y: FA-ya.
p.cinta.consejo: The c before i is th in Spain: THIN-ta.
p.excepto.consejo: The x sounds like ks, and c before e is th in Spain.
p.suspenderás.consejo: The future of «suspender» with «tú». The accent is at the end.
